title: Higher-dimensional product expansion for structured Reed–Solomon codes
formal: For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, does there exist $\rho>0$ depending only on k and epsilon with the following property? Let q be prime, let $S_i\le\mathbb F_q^\times$ have pairwise coprime sizes $s_i$, and let $C_i=\{(f(a))_{a\in S_i}:\deg f<d_i\}$ with $1\le d_i<(1-\varepsilon)s_i$. Put $\Omega=\prod_i S_i$ and let $L_i$ be the arrays on Omega whose every i-axis line belongs to $C_i$. Every $M\in\sum_i L_i$ must admit a decomposition $M=\sum_i M_i$, $M_i\in L_i$, satisfying $|\operatorname{supp}M|\ge\rho\sum_i s_i\ell_i(M_i)$, where $\ell_i$ counts nonzero i-axis lines.
context:
In two dimensions, a suitable decomposition $M=M_1+M_2$ into column and row codewords must satisfy $|\mathrm{supp}(M)|\ge\rho(n_1|M_1|_{\mathrm{col}}+n_2|M_2|_{\mathrm{row}})$.

The two-dimensional picture separates an array into contributions organized by rows and by columns. The desired inequality prevents a large amount of structured contribution from cancelling so thoroughly that the final array has very small support. The constant must work across growing block lengths.

In higher dimensions there are more directions and more ways for contributions to overlap. Good distance in each constituent code does not by itself control cancellation between these directional pieces. The question is whether the stated arithmetic structure of the evaluation sets forces a uniform expansion guarantee despite those additional interactions. Such a result must establish the full higher-dimensional decomposition inequality, not just verify individual codewords.
why: This is a specific structural obstacle to private PCPs and quantum codes supporting multiplication. The conjecture’s conditions arise from those constructions.

progress.text: The source proves the two-dimensional case. Higher dimensions remain conjectural. It also mentions an AI-generated candidate proof not verified by the authors; that is not treated here as a solution.

definitions: An i-axis line fixes all coordinates except coordinate i. Support size counts nonzero array entries; a nonzero line is one containing at least one nonzero entry. The sum of the L_i is their vector-space sum, so the assertion concerns an economical choice of decomposition, not every decomposition. Each C_i is a Reed–Solomon evaluation code of dimension d_i and rate d_i/s_i. The expansion constant must not depend on the field, subgroup sizes, or individual dimensions.
answer_criterion: Prove a positive uniform expansion constant for every fixed k and epsilon, or refute this quantified statement, for example by a family with no such positive constant for one fixed k and epsilon. A proof for k=2 or for unrelated random codes does not resolve it.

importance.reason: Higher-dimensional expansion for a structured algebraic code family is a reusable ingredient for robust tests and related constructions.
